U.note: True isometric 3D 32x32 world with terrain, nine materials, place/erase/undo and a responsive layout; clearly the richest and most block-like.

V.note: Top-down flat grid with eight colours and undo/save, but it starts blank and reads as a paint grid rather than blocks.

W.note: Only four materials on a dark empty grid with counts and a two-step clear; tidy but sparse and visually flat, and the footer is cut off on desktop.

X.note: Eight materials, a side palette, autosave and a block cap, but a dark empty 2D grid with little sense of building; the mobile palette pushes controls below the fold.

Y.note: Side-view 32x32 world with textured blocks, preloaded terrain and tree, ten tools, and a phone layout that works.

Z.note: Top-down grid with stacking to height 6 and keyboard shortcuts, but only three materials and a blank start with no depth cue.
